rationale: This is the archive's CashFundedCapexValue with the after-capex margin merely three-year-summed — a smoothing tweak of the same two ingredients rather than a substantively different mechanism.

The construction is internally incoherent because subtracting aqc/at makes heavily acquisitive firms score as "restrained" even though acquisition-driven expansion predicts low returns, and the surviving content is largely the known asset-growth anomaly crossed with the already-tested cash-to-price leg.

Moving the archived CashCapexRunwayValue from a level to a bounded change is a defensible level-versus-improvement distinction, though the delta leg is mechanically correlated with cash accumulation and thus partly redundant with the che/price gate.
This is the archive's strongest short-side signal (PriceyCapexDeficitNoBuffer) with the deficit three-year-summed — a cosmetic smoothing variant using identical components and gating structure.

Aggregating capex and inventory build into a single monotonic cash-drain measure is a genuine structural change from the prior three-way MIN gates and avoids their coverage loss, though the underlying content overlaps the accrual/investment-financing literature.

This is a mechanical recombination of components already tested in PriceyHiringCashBurnGate and PriceyDilutiveCapexDeficit, and its two non-valuation legs are the well-documented employee-growth and net-equity-issuance anomalies.
